results.name: same_decade_outside_span
results.description: For targets 1-9 outside the span of the examples, yes rate when the target shares its tens digit with some example minus when it does not; observed above null means people use decade boundaries (tens-digit grouping) more than the model predicts.
results.code:
# name: same_decade_outside_span
# description: For targets 1-9 outside the span of the examples, yes rate when the target shares its tens digit with some example minus when it does not; observed above null means people use decade boundaries (tens-digit grouping) more than the model predicts.
def _prep(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(X), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(X - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    return X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist

def _m(y, m):
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0


def test_statistic(df):
    X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist = _prep(df)
    tens = np.floor(np.mod(X, 100) / 10)
    tt = np.floor(np.mod(t, 100) / 10)
    same = np.any(tens == tt[:, None], axis=1)
    out = ((t < mn) | (t > mx)) & (dist >= 1) & (dist <= 9)
    return _m(y, out & same) - _m(y, out & ~same)

results.name: below_minus_above_near_edge_asymmetry
results.description: Yes rate for targets 1-6 below the smallest example minus yes rate for targets 1-6 above the largest example (sets of 2+ examples); observed above null means people extend ranges downward more than upward, an asymmetry the symmetric margin prior misses.
results.code:
# name: below_minus_above_near_edge_asymmetry
# description: Yes rate for targets 1-6 below the smallest example minus yes rate for targets 1-6 above the largest example (sets of 2+ examples); observed above null means people extend ranges downward more than upward, an asymmetry the symmetric margin prior misses.
def _prep(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(X), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(X - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    return X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist

def _m(y, m):
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0


def test_statistic(df):
    X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist = _prep(df)
    b = mn - t
    a = t - mx
    k = n >= 2
    return _m(y, k & (b >= 1) & (b <= 6)) - _m(y, k & (a >= 1) & (a <= 6))

results.name: parity_match_outside_span
results.description: For sets of 3+ examples that are all even or all odd, yes rate for targets outside the span with the same parity minus opposite parity; observed above null means people generalize the parity rule beyond the range more than the model predicts, below null less.
results.code:
# name: parity_match_outside_span
# description: For sets of 3+ examples that are all even or all odd, yes rate for targets outside the span with the same parity minus opposite parity; observed above null means people generalize the parity rule beyond the range more than the model predicts, below null less.
def _prep(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(X), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(X - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    return X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist

def _m(y, m):
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0


def test_statistic(df):
    X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist = _prep(df)
    par = np.where(np.isnan(X), np.nan, np.mod(X, 2))
    s = np.nansum(par, axis=1)
    alleven = (s == 0)
    allodd = (s == n)
    k = (n >= 3) & (alleven | allodd) & ((t < mn) | (t > mx))
    tp = np.mod(t, 2)
    match = (alleven & (tp == 0)) | (allodd & (tp == 1))
    return _m(y, k & match) - _m(y, k & ~match)

results.name: heading_direction_extension
results.description: For monotone (strictly ascending or descending as shown) sets of 3+ examples, yes rate for targets 1-15 beyond the end the sequence is heading toward minus beyond the end it came from; observed above null means people extrapolate in the direction of travel, which the order-blind model cannot produce.
results.code:
# name: heading_direction_extension
# description: For monotone (strictly ascending or descending as shown) sets of 3+ examples, yes rate for targets 1-15 beyond the end the sequence is heading toward minus beyond the end it came from; observed above null means people extrapolate in the direction of travel, which the order-blind model cannot produce.
def _prep(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(X), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(X - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    return X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist

def _m(y, m):
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0


def test_statistic(df):
    X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist = _prep(df)
    d = np.diff(X, axis=1)
    valid = ~np.isnan(d)
    up = np.all((d > 0) | ~valid, axis=1) & (n >= 3)
    dn = np.all((d < 0) | ~valid, axis=1) & (n >= 3)
    a = t - mx
    b = mn - t
    above = (a >= 1) & (a <= 15)
    below = (b >= 1) & (b <= 15)
    ahead = (up & above) | (dn & below)
    behind = (up & below) | (dn & above)
    return _m(y, ahead) - _m(y, behind)

results.name: wide_span_interior_yes

# description: Yes rate for non-example targets inside the span of sets of 2+ examples spanning 50 or more; observed above null means people accept broad intervals for scattered examples more than the narrow-range-favouring model predicts, below null less.
def _prep(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(float)

    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(X - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    return X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist

results.name: inspan_yes_four_minus_two_examples
results.description: Yes rate for non-example targets inside the example span, 4-example sets minus 2-example sets; observed above null means more examples raise interior acceptance more than the model predicts (model over-applies the size principle / strays for larger sets), below null the reverse.
results.code:
# name: inspan_yes_four_minus_two_examples
# description: Yes rate for non-example targets inside the example span, 4-example sets minus 2-example sets; observed above null means more examples raise interior acceptance more than the model predicts (model over-applies the size principle / strays for larger sets), below null the reverse.
def _prep(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(X), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(X - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    return X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist

def _m(y, m):
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0


def test_statistic(df):
    X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist = _prep(df)

results.name: shared_final_digit_match_far
results.description: For sets of 2+ examples all ending in the same digit, yes rate for non-example targets ending in that digit and more than 10 from every example; observed above null means people generalize the ends-in rule beyond the cluster more than the model predicts, below null less.
results.code:
# name: shared_final_digit_match_far
# description: For sets of 2+ examples all ending in the same digit, yes rate for non-example targets ending in that digit and more than 10 from every example; observed above null means people generalize the ends-in rule beyond the cluster more than the model predicts, below null less.
def _prep(df):
    X = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(X), axis=1)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    y = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    mn = np.nanmin(X, axis=1)
    mx = np.nanmax(X, axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(X - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    return X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist

def _m(y, m):
    return float(y[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0


def test_statistic(df):
    X, n, t, y, mn, mx, dist = _prep(df)
    ld = np.mod(X, 10)
    first = ld[:, 0]
    same = np.all((ld == first[:, None]) | np.isnan(ld), axis=1) & (n >= 2)
    match = np.mod(t, 10) == first
    return _m(y, same & match & (dist > 10))
